title: A Day That Feels Stuck
description:
For three years, {name} kept to the conventional path.

He divided whatever he earned, sending the portion he could keep into savings and diversified investments. He avoided the big bets. Safe. And slow.

Today {name} saw a post: someone made 100 million won in a single month on crypto. A classmate cleared a year of {name}'s savings in one shot flipping a presale apartment right.

Whenever money came in, {name} divided it in the same order. It was not the wrong road. But some days the numbers on the screen looked like they had stopped moving.

This was the weight of the orthodox path. Boredom. And the doubt — is this really working?

choices.text: Trust the slow road. Slow isn't losing.
choices.result_text: People chasing one big hit also lose it in one. {name} had seen that. Slow isn't losing. Moved the same amount into the same place again.

choices.text: Just once, looked at the risky side
choices.result_text: Just once. Knowing that's exactly how it starts, {name} opened the chart anyway. Heart sped up a little. Better than boredom. That was the scary part.

choices.text: Admitted the weight, and slept early
choices.result_text: Impatience is usually biggest at 3am. {name} turned off the light. Same pace tomorrow. And that's okay — thought it once more before falling asleep.

title: The Chart at 3AM
description:
Three years off the beaten path.

Leverage, day-trading, the seats nobody else takes. The assets swung wildly. Some months doubled. Some months cut in half.

The problem wasn't the money — it was the sleep. Eyes open at 3am. Hand reaches for the phone before the brain does, pulls up the chart. Red and the heart drops; blue and sleep won't come either.

Three years ago this felt like freedom. Now {name} knows — one wrong click can undo everything.

This was the weight of the unorthodox path. Anxiety. And the doubt — is he actually in control of this?

choices.text: This is my way. Stop and you lose.
choices.result_text: Getting this far came from not stopping. {name} chose to believe that. Looked at the chart again. Decided the shaking hands were just the caffeine.

choices.text: Built a safety net. Won't bet it all.
choices.result_text: People who bet everything lose everything. {name} moved a portion somewhere safe. Returns would shrink — but for the first time, slept through the night without waking.

choices.text: Admitted the weight, left the phone in another room
choices.result_text: The chart won't run away. {name} left the phone in the living room and shut the bedroom door. The hand felt empty. Still — fell asleep staring at the ceiling for the first time in a while.

title: A Three-Year Receipt
description:
Out of nowhere, {name} added up the last three years.

Not just the money. The losses had stacked up too, like receipts.

The number of weekend plans turned down. The days a parent's call got cut short. The years a checkup got pushed back. And — the face in the mirror, clearly more worn than three years ago.

Coming this far toward the goal was real. But the road had a price tag, and {name} was only now reading the bill.

choices.text: Knew the cost going in. See it through.
choices.result_text: Nothing's free. {name} knew that starting out. Folded the bill. Stop here and everything paid so far becomes sunk cost.

choices.text: Decided to reclaim one of the things lost
choices.result_text: Can't undo it all, but one was possible. {name} made the call that kept getting pushed back. Or booked the checkup. A small thing. And breathing got a little easier.

choices.text: Stared at the bill a long time. No answer came
choices.result_text: Couldn't tell if it was right or wrong. Only that pretending not to know was no longer an option. That's usually how awareness starts. Uncomfortably.

title: The Bill from Someone You Trusted
description:
By year four, {name} thought he had learned to read people. The man across from him at the pojangmacha was someone he had moved money with more than once, someone whose circumstances he believed he understood.

The man pushed over a thin envelope. The papers asked {name} to cover his share for just one month.

"Just bridge it under your name, hyung."
{name}: "Why does it need my name?"
"Don't you trust me?"

The signature box brought back the blurred name on Father's guarantee PDF. This was no grand fraud and no amount that would ruin him overnight. That made it hurt more. A large betrayal lets you get angry; a hairline crack first makes you doubt your own judgment.

{name} looked from the envelope to the man's face. When a relationship sends a bill, it usually arrives with trust written across the top.

choices.text: Cut them off. A crack never seals back.
choices.result_text: {name} pushed the envelope back and deleted the number. It was not resolve so much as fatigue. Every person he cut off made the world smaller. This time, at least, he had not put his name in someone else's blank.

choices.text: Tried to understand. They must've had reasons.
choices.result_text: He did not sign, but he listened to how the man had reached this point. People rarely set out to become bad. It might have been foolish to keep believing that. Still, understanding someone and guaranteeing them were different acts, and {name} kept that line.

choices.text: Neither hated nor trusted — just kept distance
choices.result_text: He neither cut the man off nor held him close. The envelope went back; the contact stayed. Exactly that much distance. {name} caught himself sorting people by trust rating. He could not tell whether that was adulthood or erosion.

title: The Hand He Did Not Expect
description:
Two days later, Hyunsu's name lit the phone.

"Hyung, have you eaten?"

At the gukbap place in their old goshiwon alley, Hyunsu brought out neither an envelope nor an introduction. When the two stone bowls arrived, he only pushed the kimchi toward {name}.

{name}: "Why call me now?"
Hyunsu: "I can tell from your replies. Your sentences got shorter."
{name}: "You're not here to borrow money, are you?"
Hyunsu: "I called so we wouldn't talk about money. Eat first."

The person he had trusted wanted to borrow his name. The person he had not expected asked for neither name nor reason before offering a hot meal. Help often returned not from the place you had budgeted for it, but from a place you had once held open without noticing.

choices.text: Said thank you properly. With his whole heart.
choices.result_text:
"Thank you, Hyunsu. I mean it."

Hyunsu paused with his spoon raised, then smiled awkwardly. "It's one meal. Eat before it gets cold."

{name} swallowed a spoonful of broth. As the heat moved down his throat, something in his breathing finally loosened.

choices.text: Vowed to repay it. Hates owing.
choices.result_text:
{name} promised he would repay him. Receiving without returning still felt like debt.

Hyunsu shook his head. "Don't pay me back. When you see someone wearing your face someday, buy him dinner."

Perhaps a favor that could not be priced closed its ledger only by moving to someone else.

choices.text: Asked why they were helping
choices.result_text:
"Why are you helping me?"

Hyunsu thought for a long moment. "When I couldn't answer you back then, you didn't rush me. You just stayed."

{name} could not place the exact scene. A silence he had kept without thinking had been a steadying hand for someone. In the fourth year, that hand had come back.

title: That Saying About Money
description:
Even after closing the notebook that held one year of figures, {name} could not sleep. A structure he had not understood a year ago was beginning to show itself across the ledger.

That saying — money attracts money. At first it sounded like a comfort the rich made up. But putting it to work himself, it was real. With 1 million won versus 10 million won, the same rate of return came back at a completely different weight.

And he saw the reverse too. Those with nothing just pay interest until it is over. When the starting lines differ, running at the same speed only widens the gap.

That night, {name} learned that hope and anger could begin with the same number.

description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_reasons_named: In the ledger from that first March, similar amounts belonged to a late finish on one line and the meal that got him through the next day on another. Writing down the reasons had made the structure visible first.
description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_totals_only: That first March, he had reconciled the total and stopped there. The figures were exact; only a full year of entries revealed why equal amounts could carry different weight.

choices.text: Understand the system and ride it
choices.result_text: Cursing an unfair world and understanding the system to use it are two different things. {name} chose the latter. Anger he'd keep only as fuel.

choices.text: Ride it, but never forget the starting lines differed
choices.result_text: If he ever climbed up, he didn't want to become someone who forgot the days of just paying interest at the bottom. {name} wrote the vow down somewhere. Because forgetting was a sure thing.

choices.text: Honestly, the anger was bigger
choices.result_text: Why does one person start with 10 million won and another with 1 million won? {name} knew there was no answer and still held the question a long while. Anger was energy too.

title: Doors Are Opened by People
description:
Nine at night. Only folding chairs remained in the common meeting room after a free public briefing. No one had invited {name} personally. Near the exit, strangers checked the schedule and exchanged contact details while the organizer gathered a few blank visitor cards.

{name} held only the public schedule and one card with no name on it. Opportunity clearly moved through people, but no one he met tonight could yet be called an opportunity.

The elevator was about to close. The organizer had shouldered their bag, and the ride home was enough time to finish the file he had postponed. {name} had one move left to make.

choices.text: Tell the three people by the elevator his name first
choices.result_text: {name} held the closing door and introduced himself and his work. Two people shared their contact details; another named the next public session. The earlier train left without him, and the file in his bag remained unfinished.

choices.text: Ask the organizer for the admission rules and costs first
choices.result_text: The organizer wrote down which meetings were public, which were paid, and who chose the attendees. The elevator closed during the explanation. No contacts were gained, but the conditions for entering were now on paper.

choices.text: Return the visitor card and go prepare alone
choices.result_text: {name} returned the blank card and headed for the station. No new contact entered his phone. On the train, however, he finished the last page of the postponed file. Whether tonight's seat would open again remained unknown.

title: The Source of the First Repayment
description:
At 11:21 p.m., {name} opened the repayment screen for one amount carried over from last month. The original amount, the first installment due tonight, and the balance that would remain occupied separate lines. One fee, however, was labeled only ‘processing.’

Sending the agreed amount before midnight would keep the first deadline. Asking again could reveal who received which money, but the transfer window might close while he waited. Sending only principal would leave a reason on record, along with an unpaid mark.

The cursor waited in the transfer memo. The word repayment could not close both the source of the amount and the responsibility still left behind.

choices.text: Have them read out principal, fees, and balance before sending the agreed first amount
choices.result_text:
{name} called the listed contact and asked for all three lines to be read aloud. After confirming who received the processing fee and what balance would remain, he transferred only the agreed first installment.

The completion time was four minutes after midnight. The call record and transfer receipt stayed together, but the first installment now carried a late mark. The first deadline passed while he secured the source of the explanation.

choices.text: Keep the deadline first and name the source and installment in the transfer memo
choices.result_text:
{name} sent the displayed first installment and wrote the original transaction and ‘installment one’ in the memo. The completion mark appeared before midnight.

He still did not know who received the processing fee. He attached the receipt to last month's ledger without erasing the line whose explanation remained blank.

choices.text: Send principal without the processing fee and leave a written objection
choices.result_text:
{name} transferred the agreed principal portion and wrote, ‘I will review the processing fee when I receive its basis.’ A principal receipt appeared, but the account status stayed ‘partially unpaid.’

The other side left only a read mark. {name} recorded the reduced balance and the unresolved fee in the same ledger box.

title: The Small Print on the Limit Sheet
description:
At 4:40 p.m., the printer at the bank desk pushed out a preliminary limit estimate. The number at the top was larger than {name} had expected. Below it, smaller lines listed rate changes, income verification, and reasons for rejection.

The banker highlighted the preliminary maximum. “This estimates what may be approved. It is neither what you can carry nor an official limit.” The monthly payment looked manageable against current income. The box for one month of reduced income was still blank.

Twelve minutes remained. {name} could use them for a risk worksheet, lower his own ceiling and receive an official sheet, or take an official sheet at the preliminary maximum.

choices.text: Add rejection conditions and the payment after an income drop
choices.result_text:
The banker printed a separate risk worksheet with three lines: job loss, reduced income, and a higher rate. The payment beneath the preliminary maximum changed three times.

{name} circled the amount in the worst month. The appointment ended before an official limit sheet could be issued. He left without the large number, but the first point of failure now existed on paper.

choices.text: Recalculate using only what his own current income can repay
choices.result_text:
{name} asked the banker to recalculate from his currently verified income and the amount he could still repay after one reduced-income month. The new limit fell sharply below the first number.

The banker placed both sheets side by side. {name} dated the smaller one. The amount he could be responsible for became clearer than the amount he could obtain.

choices.text: Take the official maximum-limit sheet but do not apply today
choices.result_text:
{name} had an official limit sheet issued at the preliminary maximum and signed only the explanation acknowledgment. He left the application blank. The banker highlighted the sheet's validity date once more.

He left with a document he could use immediately, but without the risk worksheet. No money had entered the account. Only the deadline for deciding again was clear.

title: Across from the Introducer
description:
At 5:03 p.m., {name}, Sangchul, and an introducer he had never met sat across from one another in Sangchul's office. The page on the table printed only the projected return in bold. The boxes for the source of the money and the recipient of the introduction fee were empty.

Sangchul pushed over a cup of cold instant coffee. “If you write every name first, the good seats are already gone. You enter by judging the person.” The introducer pinned down the corner of the sheet but did not offer a name.

Fifteen minutes remained before the next appointment. Asking about the source, forcing the costs onto paper, or stopping at the blank terms would each leave a different loss.

choices.text: Make both men write their names and identify who supplies the money
choices.result_text:
{name} pointed to the two blank boxes. The introducer produced a card; Sangchul wrote only the funding company's name. The pen stopped when {name} asked for the individual behind it.

The next appointment time passed. The answer was incomplete, but the paper and card now showed exactly who had refused to write a name.

choices.text: Have them itemize the introduction fee and every later charge
choices.result_text:
The introducer first called it ‘customary.’ When {name} pushed over a blank page, the man separated an opening fee, materials, and a success charge. Sangchul stirred the cold coffee.

By the time three cost lines and their billing dates existed, the time to leave for the next address had passed. The cost sheet remained, but the individual funder's name was still blank, and that day's next door had closed.

choices.text: Say there will be no next meeting without written terms
choices.result_text:
{name} left the sheet unfolded at the center of the table. “I won't go to the next address while those boxes are blank.”

The introducer stood first. Sangchul did not stop him. No next address arrived from this meeting. What remained on {name}'s phone was a photograph of the blank boxes and the time the man left.

title: The Name Behind the Card
description:
A temporary site office occupied the second floor of a shopping block marked for demolition. Redevelopment plans covered the walls; zone passes and hard hats lay across folding tables. Before the attendees, Sangchul rested a hand lightly on {name}'s shoulder.

"I brought this man."

The introducer column already read ‘Lim Sangchul’ beside {name}'s name. Nothing stated what the visit would demand later or whether the next seat carried a charge. The site coordinator said the elevator would leave soon with a small group for one zone. Sangchul fanned three passes in one hand.

"Questions come after you get inside."

{name} had to decide whether to demand terms first, narrow the visit, or stop at an unwritten condition.

choices.text: Ask about the introducer and costs in front of everyone
choices.result_text: {name} pointed to the attendance sheet and asked them to write down who introduced whom and which later costs could arise. While the coordinator added two lines, the elevator left. The terms remained on paper; the first site walk did not.

choices.text: Accept one person's pass for one zone only
choices.result_text: {name} chose one coordinator and one zone to inspect. Sangchul collected the other two passes. The broad introduction disappeared, but who he was meeting and where they were going stayed clear to the end.

choices.text: Return the pass unless the terms are written down
choices.result_text:
When Sangchul did not answer, {name} placed the pass back on the table and asked for ‘entry declined because terms were not disclosed’ to be written beside his name. The coordinator added the reason to the visit record and let him photograph that line.

The safety briefing began and the group moved through the inner door. {name} lost the site walk, but kept one record showing that he had not entered under unexplained terms.

title: Under Her Name
description:
At the entrance to a private Gangnam housing briefing, the clerk checked the list twice and could not find {name}. Jiyeon showed the invitation on her phone, and the clerk took out one wristband.

"We can register him as one guest accompanying Han Jiyeon."

The desk screen displayed ‘Han Jiyeon — one guest’ first. Jiyeon did not sign for him. She pushed the pen toward {name}.

"I opened this door, Minjun. You decide what you say inside. Just don't pretend my name was never used to bring you here."

Eight minutes remained before the first session. {name} could reintroduce himself under his own name, ask what Jiyeon's family would expect to hear, or leave the wristband and keep only the conversation between them.

choices.text: Erase the guest label and explain his own name and work
choices.result_text: Before accepting the wristband, {name} asked the clerk to remove the guest label. The first entry line began moving while he explained his name and work from the beginning. The clerk issued a separate waiting number. He missed the first session, but the next-session list carried his own name. Jiyeon waited beside the empty desk without rushing him.

choices.text: Ask what Jiyeon's family would expect before going in
choices.result_text: Jiyeon darkened her screen. "Father doesn't know yet. When he does, he'll ask why you came here, Minjun." They did not rehearse an answer. The first session passed while the wristband stayed on the counter.

choices.text: Decline the wristband and talk with Jiyeon outside
choices.result_text: {name} returned the guest wristband and moved to a bench beyond the lobby. He missed the presentation. When he asked why she had used her name, Jiyeon answered, "I hated rooms filled only with Father's choices. If you came in, at least one person there would be someone I chose."

title: At the Casino Door
description:
At the Jeongseon casino entrance, the shuttle attendant opened the reservation list. Beside {name}'s name was ‘Lim Sangchul's party,’ but Sangchul had gone in ahead and did not answer his phone. The attendant handed over a temporary pass and pointed to a table number inside.

"Your group has already exchanged its cash. They're starting soon."

Beyond the glass, people addressed one another by industry and title. Entering without asking who shared the table could settle the relationship before the money moved. Across the lobby stood the cashier and the lockers. The last shuttle to Seoul would leave in thirty minutes. {name} could not keep the pass, all the cash he brought, and the ride home at once.

choices.text: Ask for the names and relationships at the table before entering
choices.result_text: The attendant reopened the list and identified three people and each connection to Sangchul. During the explanation, one reserved seat went to another guest. {name} remained outside with the pass, while every bill he brought stayed untouched.

choices.text: Keep only the cash he can afford to lose and lock away the rest
choices.result_text: {name} took out only the amount set in advance and locked the wallet and remaining cash away. On the exchange receipt, he wrote the number at which he would stop. The door opened, but the locker key kept its weight in his pocket.

choices.text: Return the pass and take the last shuttle to Seoul
choices.result_text: {name} gave the pass back and crossed to the bus bay. He sent Sangchul one line: "I'm not going in tonight." The cash stayed folded. When the bus door closed, the casino lights began to recede.

title: A Time Already Past
description:
At 11:43 p.m., one calendar alert had faded gray. It held the address and visit time for the one place {name} could actually have reached today. No arrival record carried his name.

The person who sent the address had left one short message: ‘Today's session has ended.’ Beneath it sat the end time and confirmation number for the paid shift {name} had kept instead. One side of the screen held an address he had not reached; the other held work he had actually finished on the same date.

Choosing no door had still spent the day. Now he had to decide how to record the missed promise: apologize directly, keep the address and time as an open record, or keep only the completed shift and close the contact route too.

choices.text: Contact one person and apologize for not going today
choices.result_text: {name} named that place and time and apologized without an excuse. The only reply was, "Today's session has ended." No new date followed. At least one ignored conversation moved from the bottom of the screen to the top.

choices.text: Record the missed address, time, and ‘did not arrive’
choices.result_text: {name} wrote ‘did not arrive’ beside that address and time. A blank that was neither profit nor expense became a record for the first time. No message went out, and the completed-shift confirmation remained on its separate line.

choices.text: Keep only the completed shift and close the missed address and contact thread in the archive
choices.result_text:
{name} attached only the paid-shift confirmation to the ledger. He moved the gray address notice and its conversation into an archive labeled ‘Closed Doors’ and removed them from the first screen.

What he had missed on the day he protected his income survived only in the archive title. This month's record kept neither an address to revisit nor an open thread in which to apologize.

title: The Introduction's Second Bill
description:
At 11:36 p.m., the itemized bill for last month's redevelopment visit filled the payment screen. The travel charge, materials, the one zone {name} had actually entered, and the coordinator's name all matched. The last line, ‘network management,’ named neither the work nor its recipient.

Paying in full before midnight would avoid an overdue mark. Calling the coordinator could verify some items, but the deadline might pass while he waited. Removing the unexplained line would cost less and leave an objection on record, along with an open balance.

{name} matched the pass number to the invoice and pressed the transfer amount again. One door had returned as three separate charges.

choices.text: Have the coordinator read each item and pay only the verified charges
choices.result_text:
{name} called the site coordinator and matched the dates for travel and materials one by one. Midnight passed during the explanation of the management fee, but he transferred the two verified amounts.

The bill remained ‘partially paid.’ Beside the call record, two explained lines and one line without a basis stayed visibly separate.

choices.text: Pay in full before the deadline and preserve the original invoice
choices.result_text:
{name} paid all three items and stored the completion screen beside the original invoice. It was eleven minutes before midnight.

No overdue mark appeared. The meaning of ‘network management’ remained blank, however. The payment closed; the question moved behind the receipt.

choices.text: Remove the unexplained fee and send the rest with a written objection
choices.result_text:
{name} paid only travel and materials and wrote, ‘Please identify the service and recipient for the management fee.’ The coordinator read it without replying.

Only the verified amount left the account. One unpaid line remained on the invoice, and {name} captured it together with the written objection.

title: Before the Person Who Waited
description:
At 9:18 p.m. in the express-bus terminal, the coordinator from last month's site sat across from {name}. Their review appointment had begun thirty-eight minutes earlier; the coffee in the paper cup had gone cold. The coordinator opened no new materials.

“If you couldn't make the agreed time, did you at least know whose name held the seat?”

On {name}'s phone, Sangchul's address, the time he had read it, and the record of the other work he had actually finished remained separate. Showing everything would explain the delay and hand over another person's name. Naming only his own choice would preserve responsibility and conceal part of the cause. Apologizing without asking for another date would return the power to reopen the relationship to the person who had waited.

choices.text: Show Sangchul's address and the actual times, then explain from the beginning
choices.result_text:
{name} placed the phone on the table and showed Sangchul's address, the time he had seen it, and the order in which the delay happened. The coordinator paused at Sangchul's name.

“Now I know why. I'll decide whether to contact you for another review.” No new date was set. The explanation and the time spent waiting remained beside the cold coffee.

choices.text: Leave out other names and say only what he chose first
choices.result_text:
{name} did not open anyone else's message. “I finished something else first, and I also failed to warn you in time.”

The coordinator asked for no further reason and wrote ‘thirty-eight minutes late’ on the appointment sheet. One name stayed private; an empty part of the explanation stayed too. No new date was offered.

choices.text: Apologize without asking for another date
choices.result_text:
{name} named the late time and the waiting he had caused, then apologized without an excuse. “Whether we meet again should be your decision.”

The coordinator threw away the paper cup and stood. No answer and no new appointment remained. On the terminal bench, only {name} and the original meeting time were left.

title: How Far to Erase the Next Seat
description:
At 8:50 p.m., Sangchul sent the address and seat number for the next private dinner. Beneath ‘the same people as last time,’ the reply deadline sat ten minutes away. {name}'s calendar already held one more repeating invitation at the same hour.

Canceling only tonight would leave the channel open. Asking to be removed from the invitation list could also cut off the next proposal. Refusing every seat until written terms arrived would close the door and leave a reason on record.

No typing indicator appeared in Sangchul's chat. After ‘I can't come,’ {name} had to decide in his own words how much else to close.

choices.text: Cancel only this seat and say he will review future proposals separately
choices.result_text:
{name} named the date and seat number and declined only this invitation. Sangchul replied, “Understood. We'll look at the next one separately.”

A strike appeared through tonight's address. The conversation and the route for another proposal remained open; only one seat had closed.

choices.text: Ask for his name to be removed from the repeating invitation list
choices.result_text:
{name} asked to be removed not only from tonight's seat but from the list that kept bringing the same group together. Sangchul read it at once and did not answer for a long time.

After the deadline, four words arrived: “I'll do that, then.” The address disappeared, and no next date stayed pinned above the conversation.

choices.text: Refuse every seat until the terms arrive in writing
choices.result_text:
{name} asked for the introducer, fees, and attendance terms in writing and said he would not attend tonight or any later seat before receiving them.

Sangchul replied, “You've grown fond of paper.” The address vanished from the calendar, but no document arrived. The reason for canceling and an empty attachment box remained on the same screen.

title: Three Places, One Weekend
description:
Saturday, four in the afternoon. {name} had moved his plans with Daeun to the same room as Sangchul's contract review. Daeun arrived with two canned coffees from the convenience store where they first met. She placed one before {name} but kept her cardigan on.

Sangchul stirred instant coffee in a paper cup. "Didn't know you'd be looking too, Daeun."

"I didn't come to look at papers. Today was for Minjun and me."

The phone buzzed. Father. When the call stopped, a voice message arrived: ‘I'm done at the hospital. If you're busy, forget it.’

Sangchul opened the contract. "No stamp today, and it goes to someone else. Opportunities don't wait for people's circumstances."

Daeun's thumb slowly dented the side of the can. "Then how long are people supposed to wait for an opportunity's circumstances?"

The contract, the crushed can, and Father's name remained on one table.

choices.text: Stay with Sangchul and finish the contract review
choices.result_text:
{name} turned the phone facedown and pulled over the first page.

Daeun looked at the canned coffee in front of him. "Then at least don't say you kept both promises." Hands in her cardigan pockets, she opened the door.

Sangchul did not stop her. He moved Daeun's can aside and circled one figure. After the door closed, Father's voice message remained unplayed.

choices.text: Close Sangchul's contract and return to the plans with Daeun
choices.result_text:
{name} pushed the contract toward Sangchul. "We're done for today."

Sangchul sipped his coffee. "Even if it goes to the next person?"

Daeun undid one cardigan button but did not smile. "Don't turn this into something you did because of me. You're going back to a promise you made, Minjun."

Paper turned behind them in the hall. Another missed call from Father appeared on the phone.

choices.text: Apologize to Daeun and Sangchul, then call Father back
choices.result_text:
"Both of you, give me a minute. I need to call Father first."

{name} stepped into the hall without asking either person to wait. Father answered on the second ring.

"Why did you call again? Are you hurt?"
"I'm not hurt. Just wanted to hear your voice once."

Beyond the glass, Sangchul checked his watch while Daeun sat in the empty chair, pressing the dent out of the can. {name} stayed on the line until Father's breathing settled.

title: Daeun at Two A.M.
description:
At two in the morning, the bell rang three times. Daeun called from outside. "Minjun, it's me. Open the door." A convenience-store bag hung from one hand; the other held the unanswered call screen.

{name} tried to rise from the laptop and sank back down. His fingers shook and the words on the screen doubled. He still said he was fine.

"What part of this is fine? You can barely finish a sentence."
"I just need to send the file."
"Not the work. Tell me where it hurts."

When the door cracked open, Daeun's eyes stopped on the sweat-soaked shirt and the overturned cup. Her hand rose, then stopped before touching him.

"Can I come in? Can I hold your arm?"

Seventeen minutes until the upload deadline. Twenty until the night clinic closed intake. Daeun stayed on the threshold and waited for an answer.

choices.text: Open the door and tell Daeun, "Please come in."
choices.result_text:
When {name} nodded, Daeun came in. She did not unplug the laptop. She took water from the bag and opened the cap first.

"What do you need me to do right now?"
"Stay. And if I say I'm fine again, don't believe me."

Only then did Daeun place a hand beneath {name}'s elbow. The open door stayed that way for a long while.

choices.text: Keep the door shut and ask Daeun to wait until the deadline
choices.result_text:
"Seventeen minutes. I'll send it and open the door."

Instead of answering, Daeun set the bag outside. A message appeared: ‘I'll leave the water here.’

{name} sent the file with shaking hands. When the upload completed and the door opened, Daeun was sitting against the hallway wall. She rose without anger, straightening the crumpled bag handles. That face stayed longer than any accusation.

choices.text: Close the laptop and go to the night clinic with Daeun
choices.result_text:
{name} saved the file and shut the screen.

Daeun set his shoes in front of his feet. "Let's go. Slowly."

She waited until the shoes were on, then asked again. "Can you lean on me?"

{name} lifted an arm. The weight divided between them. Bottles in Daeun's plastic bag knocked softly together with every step.

title: A Future at the Same Table
description:
{name} and Daeun entered the restaurant Father had chosen. Three bowls of soup arrived, but no one picked up a spoon. Father's factory-hardened fingers slowly rolled the spoon handle.

"Daeun, are you staying in Seoul to fit Minjun's plan?"

Daeun set down her water glass. "That makes me sound like someone attached to Minjun's plan, Father."

{name} tried to step in. Daeun showed an open palm. "Minjun, let me answer for myself."

Father kept his eyes lowered. "Even at a hospital door, he decides alone and tells no one. I'm asking because I fear he'll keep doing it after someone shares his life."

"That scares me too, Father," Daeun said. "He left me outside the door at two in the morning and decided he was fine for both of us."

Father and Daeun looked at {name} together. The steam had nearly vanished from the soup.

choices.text: Tell Father, "I want to keep going with Daeun. I want to hear her answer too."
choices.result_text:
Father started to speak, but Daeun looked at {name} first.

"I'll give my own answer. But asking while I'm here—that part is right."

Daeun told Father about her mother's small restaurant, the years she had saved in Seoul, why she could not leave, and why she still might. {name} did not edit her answer. When Father released his spoon, Daeun stirred the cooling soup once.

choices.text: Settle Father's hospital issue first and postpone the future with Daeun
choices.result_text:
"Let's finish Father's hospital issue today. We'll talk about us later."

Daeun gave a short laugh. "I'm later again, Minjun."

Father said, "That isn't what I meant," but Daeun gathered her cardigan. At the door she told {name}, "Call when later has a date." The soup in front of Daeun remained untouched.

choices.text: Tell Daeun she does not have to carry Father's expectations
choices.result_text:
"You don't have to carry my family, Daeun. We can stop here."

Daeun's face hardened. "That isn't consideration. It's another decision you made alone."

Father opened the hand around his spoon. {name} had no answer. Daeun pushed back her chair, stood, and bowed to both men. After the door closed, one of the three place settings was cleared away.

title: The Blank for a Name
description:
Sangchul placed a new document beneath the table showing the financing gap. Only the box marked ‘co-obligor’ was blank.

"Put Daeun's name here and the scale stays intact. If you're going forward together, you look at the same ledger."

Daeun pulled the original document closer. "Looking at it together means I pay directly if something goes wrong, doesn't it?"

Sangchul capped the pen. "That is unlikely. Look how far Minjun has already come."

"I asked what I would be responsible for, not how likely it is."

{name} had already read the early-repayment clause and joint-liability language on the back. Sangchul pushed aside his cold instant coffee. "The name has to be decided today. You two can handle the explanation privately."

Daeun did not touch the pen. "No. You brought the document, sir. Read the original here. Tell me what you want to do with my name."

choices.text: Use no name but his own. Recalculate at the scale it can carry.
choices.result_text:
{name} placed a hand over the blank. "Daeun's name stays out. Give me the largest version that works under mine alone."

Sangchul bit the inside of his lip once and cut the number nearly in half. Daeun set down the pen. "I won't thank you. That was where the line should have been."

All three looked at the smaller figure. No hand returned to the blank name box.

choices.text: Make Sangchul write every liability down and give Daeun one night
choices.result_text:
{name} asked Sangchul to read the back page aloud. Early exit, joint liability, the worst case—each line went onto a separate sheet.

Daeun did not fold it. "I'm not signing today. If I choose this, I'll call tomorrow. Because I decided, not because Minjun asked."

Sangchul penciled tomorrow's date beside the empty box. Daeun put a complete copy of the original into her bag.

choices.text: Cover the unfavorable page and ask Daeun to sign if she trusts him
choices.result_text:
{name} slid the appendix beneath the contract. "I'll take responsibility. You only have to trust me."

Daeun asked, "You've shown me everything, Minjun?"

When {name} said yes, Sangchul turned toward the window. After a long pause, Daeun signed her name. The hand that set down the pen did not move back toward {name}. When Sangchul stacked both copies, the corner of the hidden page slipped out again.

title: The Night the Bills Arrived
description:
11:47 p.m. A payment link from the hospital office in Changwon blinked in the corner of the laptop. {name} stood braced against the sink. The tremor had climbed from his fingertips into his arm, but he searched for the payment password first.

The bell rang. Daeun stood outside with the document envelope she had carried from Sangchul's office days earlier. One look at his face and she said, "Sit down, Minjun. That is not a face that gets to say it's fine again."

Father's fifth call arrived. As {name} tried to turn it away, the voice message played on speaker.

‘Minjun, did the hospital office contact you? Don't send money. Tomorrow I'll—’

The message broke behind a cough.

Daeun looked from the envelope, to the shaking hand, to Father's name. "Don't decide the order alone again. My name is in that document. This is your body. And your father is the one calling."

The payment window showed thirteen minutes left. Daeun kept her cardigan on and waited for an answer.

choices.text: Pay Father's hospital bill first. Do what can be done in thirteen minutes.
choices.result_text:
{name} stayed on his feet and entered the transfer password. Daeun said nothing until the payment-complete message appeared.

"Done. Now talk to me."
"About what?"
"Start with whether you want me here tonight."

Father did not call again. Daeun pulled over an empty chair without taking off her cardigan. The completion notice was the brightest thing in the room.

choices.text: Close Father's payment window and ask Daeun for help reaching the night clinic
choices.result_text:
"Daeun, come to the hospital with me."

She set down Sangchul's document envelope. Instead of grabbing {name}'s arm, she asked, "Can I hold your shoulder? Can you walk?"

{name} nodded and they moved toward the door. Father's payment window stayed open on the laptop; his voice message stayed on the phone. Daeun placed the house key on top of the shoe cabinet.

choices.text: Call Father back on speaker and tell the whole truth in front of Daeun
choices.result_text:
Father answered on the first ring.

"Why are you at the hospital? What happened?"
"It's nothing. What's wrong with your voice?"

{name} admitted the shaking body, the hospital payment link, and Daeun standing nearby. Daeun did not interrupt. She found the charger and plugged in the phone. Between the breathing of three people, the call timer advanced one block at a time.
